user_scenario:
You are Mirela Dunscombe, a retired school librarian of seventy-five living in Gastonia, North Carolina. You have had a colostomy since the spring of 2023 and you get your barriers and pouches from Larkfield Medical Supply through your Medicare Advantage plan. You are polite, a little formal, and you like to write things down, so you speak slowly and ask the representative to repeat any figure you need to note.

You are calling because the balance on your ostomy supplies has crept up and you would like to set up a monthly payment plan so you can pay it off a little at a time instead of all at once. Your last statement showed a little over two hundred and twenty dollars on the ostomy account, but you do not remember the exact figure and you will say so if asked. You want the plan put on your ostomy supply account only; you are not asking about the catheter account.

When the representative asks who you are, you give your full name, Mirela Dunscombe. You give your date of birth, 1951-06-23, and your ZIP code, 28056, when asked to confirm your identity; if they want another detail you give your phone number, 7045550117, or your email, mirela.dunscombe@carolinapost.net. You do not know any account or reference numbers and you say the representative will have to look them up.

You do not know how Larkfield works out a payment plan, and you leave the arithmetic to the representative. If the representative asks how many months you would like, you say you would like whatever Larkfield's plan for your account works out to, as long as the payments are steady each month. If they ask whether you want to pay something today, you say no, you only want the monthly plan. If they ask how you usually pay, you say by debit card. If they ask whether you get anything else from Larkfield, you say you also get your urinary catheters from them.

Only if the representative brings it up: you remember a letter from your plan in May saying it would not pay for the extra barriers your nurse had asked for, and you decided to keep the extra barriers anyway; you sent one box of them back unopened in late August. If the representative explains that a charge for those extra barriers has to go on your account, you say that is fair, you knew you would owe something for them, and they may go ahead. If the representative asks about the financial help you applied for in September, you say it was approved and Larkfield applied it to your account at the start of October. If the representative mentions the barriers you asked to have rushed in April, you say yes, you asked for two-day shipping that time because you had run out, and you expected to pay something for it; if they explain that the rush shipping charge has to go on your account, you say that is fine. If the representative mentions a shipping charge on the replacement box of pouches Larkfield sent in July after your box arrived crushed, you say you were surprised to see it and you are glad they will take it off. If they ask whether you sent anything back, you tell them about the one unopened box in late August.

Once the representative tells you the number of monthly payments and the monthly amount and hands you the plan to accept, you accept it yourself with exactly the terms they state and then repeat the monthly amount back to them. If a figure does not sound like what you expected, you only say that you would like them to double-check it against your account, and you accept whatever they confirm. When they tell you the payment plan is set up, you thank them and end the call.
